reviews.review:
A Souls-Like With a Shotgun to Your Head (In the Best Possible Way)
Remnant 2 opens exactly where you’d expect a “souls game with guns” to begin: it drop-kicks you into boss fights that look like H.R. Giger’s fever dreams and politely reminds you that the floor is your only checkpoint. It’s tough at first—no sugar-coating that—but the moment you discover your combo of archetype + weapon mod + mutator, the gameplay turns to butter. Dual-classing is the secret sauce: pair an Engineer turret with Hunter crit chains and suddenly you’re John Wick in an interdimensional maze.

Co-op: The Real Final Boss Is Your Sleep Schedule
Solo is satisfying; co-op is a black hole for free time. Enemy scaling feels fair, roles dovetail perfectly (one player stacks DoTs, another staggers, another heals), and the lack of friendly fire saves friendships. “I’ll just do one more run” reliably morphs into “Why is the sun coming up?”

Replayability Off the Charts—Literally
Procedural Worlds: Every Campaign or Adventure reroll shuffles biomes, dungeons, and minibosses. That secret .50 cal room? Might not exist in your seed.

DLC That Actually Matters:

The Awakened King adds Losomn nightmares, new loot, and the Ritualist archetype.

The Forgotten Kingdom turns Yaesha into a living jungle and introduces the Invoker.

A third expansion is still on the roadmap, already included if you grabbed the bundle.

Endgame That Feels Like a Beginning: Finish the campaign, unlock Apocalypse difficulty, and the game whispers, “That was just the tutorial.”

Five Reasons Souls Fans Will Love It
Challenge Without Despair – Tweaking builds is a built-in rage diffuser.

AAA Gunfeel – Every trigger pull has weight; reload animations are chef’s-kiss.

FromSoft-Style Lore – Environmental storytelling, cryptic NPCs, multi-ending bosses.

Drop-In/Out Co-op – Seamless joins, shared progression, perfect for LAN nights.

Hundreds of Hours of Secrets – After 300+ hours I’m still stumbling into hidden rooms and weapons.

Verdict
Remnant 2 is the happy marriage of souls-like tension and modern shooter adrenaline: brutal at the start, silky-smooth once your build clicks. If you want a game that turns “quick session” into epic all-nighters, look no further. I’ve recommended it to dozens of friends—none of them have managed to peel themselves away from the monitor yet.

TL;DR: Buy it with your eyes closed—or better, wide open through the scope. See you in the Labyrinth! 🎯

Great game, best when played with 2 friends, but 1 works too. First playthrough may be a bit clunky, but as soon as you get a build going, the game really opens up, so don't give up early (that being before playing through the campaign once)!

That being said, don't stop playing after winning once, the game is designed for you to play multiple campaigns and adventures on one character, don't miss out by ignoring that feature.

In conclusion, the game's great, even when solo (though way harder), there's a lot of build variety and (at the point of writing this) 3 DLCs to bite your teeth out on, or just to find all the secrets on a lower difficulty.

9/10, not quite Elden Ring with guns, but pretty darn close.
